dedupe_keys.name: university community acceptance of urine recycling in sixteen countries

description: This collection contains 3,763 anonymous survey responses about using human urine as crop fertilizer, collected in 2017–2018 at twenty universities in sixteen countries. Melissa Barton and collaborators designed the survey to assess food-consumer acceptance and barriers to source-separated sanitation. Demographics, perceived risks and benefits, social norms, willingness to pay and environmental attitudes accompany questions on recycling options. Mendeley provides raw and cleaned Excel data, translated questionnaires and a PDF codebook, free under CC BY 4.0. Cleaned coded responses are translated into English, while some open comments retain their original language. University-community participation limits population representativeness, and stated willingness does not establish actual purchasing or sanitation adoption. A reviewer-assessed use is parameterizing acceptance assumptions in household-agent or sanitation-transition simulations. model-citydrain3-integrated-urban-drainage-toolbox offers related physical sanitation modelling, at a different level of analysis. No respondent data were downloaded or behavioural model fitted.
